lead: Valencia is a flat city, with more than 160 km of cycle lanes, an integrated public transport network and several options for discovering the city comfortably, sustainably and economically.

Valencia is one of the most convenient cities in Spain for getting around without a car. Its completely flat terrain, a cycle-lane network of more than 160 kilometres, the Valenbisi public bike service and integrated public transport between bus, metro and tram make any point in the city reachable in a few minutes.
The Valencia Tourist Card includes unlimited transport on bus, metro, tram and commuter train, plus free admission to the municipal museums and discounts at the main attractions.

items.title: EMT · City bus
items.body: The Municipal Transport Company of Valencia operates the most comprehensive city bus network, with more than 60 lines covering all the neighbourhoods, the beaches, the Albufera and the surrounding area. The system runs 24 hours with night lines (N lines) and is the most accessible way to reach any point in Valencia without needing to change.
facts: Direct lines to Malvarrosa in summer
Lines 24 and 25 · Free with the Tourist Card
EMT Valencia: real time at every stop
The whole city · More than 60 lines
The Móbilis card integrates bus, metro and Valenbisi on a single card. Avoid paying for single tickets.

items.title: Metrovalencia · Metro and tram
items.body: The Metrovalencia network combines metro, tram and commuter train in an integrated system with 9 lines and 156 stations. It connects the centre with the outlying neighbourhoods, the airport (lines 3 and 5), the marina, the Comunitat Valenciana and the municipalities of the metropolitan area. Lines 3 and 5 connect the airport directly with the centre in about 25 minutes.
facts: From €1.50 depending on zones · Free with the Tourist Card
Lines 3 and 5 · 25 min to the centre
L3/L5 Nou d’Octubre or Av. del Cid stop
Tram L4 · La Marina or Las Arenas stop
notes: Lines L3 and L5 serve the airport. It is the fastest and cheapest way to reach the centre from the airport: 25 min for €1.50.

items.title: Valenbisi · Public bike
items.body: Valenbisi is Valencia’s municipal bike-sharing service, running since 2010 and managed by JCDecaux. With 2,750 bikes spread over 276 stations across the city, it is one of the densest public bike networks in Spain. The first 30 minutes of each journey are free with any pass, making it the cheapest urban transport for short trips.
facts: €13.30 · Unlimited for 7 days · 30 min free per journey
€29.21 · Unlimited for 12 months · 30 min free per journey
notes: If your journey is under 30 minutes, Valenbisi is completely free with any pass. Return the bike to a station and take it out again for longer journeys at no extra cost.

items.title: Private bike rental
items.body: Several companies offer bike rental in Valencia without Valenbisi’s time restrictions, with options of city bikes, e-bikes, mountain bikes and tandems. Ottowheels is one of the leading companies, with rental of bikes and electric scooters and guided tours of the city. The company Brompton Junction offers the popular folding bikes to take on public transport.
facts: From €10/day · No time or station restrictions
From €15/day · Ideal for couples and families
Brompton Junction · To combine with metro or bus
Rental + guided bike and electric scooter tours
notes: If you will be spending more than a day in Valencia and want total freedom, private rental is more convenient than Valenbisi for long itineraries or ones with stops far from stations.

items.title: Tourist Bus · The Red Bus
items.body: Valencia’s Tourist Bus, known as The Red Bus, covers the city’s main attractions on two routes with open-top double-decker buses. The 24- or 48-hour ticket lets you hop on and off at the 17 stops as often as you like. It is the only means of transport with an open upper deck, ideal for taking photos and getting your bearings on your first day in the city. Discounts with the Valencia Tourist Card.
facts: 17 stops · IVAM, Mestalla, CAC, Oceanogràfic, Bioparc and more
Included in the ticket in several languages
Approx. €30 · Unlimited access for two days
2 routes · 17 stops · The whole centre and beaches
notes: On your first day in Valencia, the Tourist Bus is the most efficient way to get your bearings in the city. Take the 24 h ticket and use it to decide which places you want to visit in more depth the next day.

items.title: Segway · Guided tours
items.body: Segway tours are a fun and different way of getting around Valencia. Segway Trip Valencia offers guided routes through the historic centre, the Turia Garden, the Serranos Towers and other emblematic places in the city. The tours include about 15 minutes of prior training to learn to ride the vehicle and are suitable for people with no previous experience.
facts: 1 h – 2 h depending on the chosen route
Historic centre, Turia Garden, coast and beaches
15 min of practice included before the route
Online booking in advance is essential
notes: Segway tours of the old town and the Serranos Towers are especially popular at sunset. Book at least a day in advance.

items.title: Electric scooters · Ottowheels
items.body: Ottowheels is the leading operator for electric scooter rental in Valencia, committed to sustainable tourism. As well as free rental, it offers guided scooter tours of the city’s most emblematic and lesser-known corners. Electric scooters are allowed on cycle lanes and cycle streets, which makes getting around the Turia Garden and the historic centre very easy.
facts: Driving licence or ID card · Over 16s
Helmet compulsory · Cycle lanes and cycle streets only
Acciona, Yego and Cooltra: motorbike sharing by the minute
notes: Electric scooters are banned on pavements and in pedestrian areas. The Turia Garden has a continuous 9 km cycle lane that is ideal for scooter rides.

blocks.title: Tips for getting around Valencia
items: The Tourist Card includes unlimited transport from €15.30: worth it from day one
Valenbisi has 276 stations: the first 30 min of each journey are free with any pass
The metro reaches the airport in 25 min for €1.50 — the cheapest option from the airport
The Turia Garden has 9 km of continuous cycle lane with no traffic lights or crossings with cars
Bus lines 24 and 25 reach the Albufera and are free with the Tourist Card
Tram L4 connects the centre directly with the Malvarrosa beaches
